To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a novel analog/RF spatial filter is presented that can achieve arbitrary spatial filtering in the RF domain and that can be used in digital MIMO receivers to reduce the dynamic range requirements of the following analog/RF front-end.

we propose a new technique for arbitrary spatial filtering in MIMO receiver arrays, which is based on frequency-translational analog/RF filtering, and which allows the synthesis and steering of an arbitrary set of spatial notches at baseband and/or RF.

a novel arbitrary spatial filtering technique is proposed that can generate an arbitrary number of notches, and that the technique is implemented in a 65-nm test chip and verified with wireless measurements.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new class of MIMO receiver array architectures that can provide spatial filtering in the analog/ RF domain, and thus enable the use of digital MIMO receivers in practical applications.

the development of a spatial filter that allows the synthesis of arbitrary spatial filtering response at RF, and is suitable for integration into the RF front end of digital MIMO receiver arrays to protect the following analog-to digital converters from high instantaneous dynamic range analog/RF spatial signals.
the design and implementation of a novel spatial filtering technique, which can provide arbitrary notch filtering in both the analog and RF domains for MIMO receiver arrays.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper presents a novel analog/RF spatial notching scheme that allows arbitrary spatial filtering at baseband as well as RF.
the proposed arbitrary spatial filtering technique is a novel and effective solution to the analog/RF dynamic range problem of digital MIMO receivers.
the proposed arbitrary spatial filtering technique provides a practical solution for the protection of digital MIMO receiver arrays from spatial interference.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated the first arbitrary spatial analog/RF filtering technique for digital MIMO receiver arrays, and the technique has been demonstrated to be effective for protecting the following ADCs and improving the in-band linearity performance of the receiver.

the arbitrary spatial filtering technique is the first of its kind to provide arbitrary spatial filtering in the analog/ RF domain, and the first to provide arbitrary spatial notching in the RF domain.

we have demonstrated an arbitrary spatial filtering technique in a MIMO receiver array, and the technique is able to provide sufficient filtering to the following ADCs while maintaining high linearity and noise performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
arbitrary spatial filtering can be realized with a simple and efficient circuit architecture that can be integrated into the receiver array.
the arbitrary spatial filtering technique can be implemented in a fully integrated CMOS receiver array and can be easily integrated with the following analog-to- digital conversion stages.

the proposed frequency-translational spatial filtering technique can be used to protect the following analog-to- digital converter from spatial interference and relax the stringent dynamic range requirement of the analog-to-digital converter.
